key_insight: Asymptomatic female carriers of the XDP-associated TAF1 variant showed clear striatal neurodegeneration and increased caudate iron on MRI, even without overt movement or cognitive symptoms.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest that female XDP carriers may harbor subclinical brain changes that could be relevant for future risk stratification and longitudinal monitoring.
method: 103 female relatives of XDP patients were assessed and classified as 42 female mutation carriers and 61 healthy controls.
Participants underwent clinical testing plus multimodal MRI, including T1 structural imaging, voxel-based morphometry, subcortical volumetry, and susceptibility-weighted imaging.
A subset had follow-up MRI over up to 25.5 months to look for progression.
evidence_signal: Compared with controls, carriers had significantly smaller caudate, putamen, and pallidum volumes (all p<0.001) and higher caudate iron signal, with stronger atrophy linked to more iron deposition.
watch_item: The study was observational with limited longitudinal follow-up, so it cannot determine how quickly these changes progress or whether they predict future symptoms.
paper_title: Preclinical Basal Ganglia Neurodegeneration in Female X Linked Dystonia Parkinsonism Carriers
